pairs.prompt: Write a practical six-step guide to setting up a comfortable home workspace in a small room. Cover location, chair and screen position, lighting, cables, supplies, and a daily reset. Explain the reasons for your suggestions, include low-cost alternatives, and make the whole guide useful to someone starting from scratch.
pairs.neutral:
1. Choose a location
Pick a quiet corner with enough room to sit and move comfortably. Keep the doorway clear and avoid blocking a shared route. If a separate desk will not fit, use one end of a dining table and agree when that space is available.

2. Set your sitting position
Adjust the chair so your feet rest on the floor or a stable box. Keep your shoulders relaxed and the keyboard close enough to avoid reaching. Raise the screen toward eye level with a sturdy stand or books; use a separate keyboard if raising a laptop.

3. Arrange the light
Place the screen sideways to a window to reduce glare. Add a modest task lamp if the room is dim, aiming it at the work surface rather than the display. Check the setup at the time of day when you normally work and adjust curtains as needed.

4. Route the cables
Group charging and display cables along the back of the table with reusable ties. Leave enough slack to move equipment without pulling plugs. Keep cables away from walkways and water, and avoid overloading sockets. Label similar chargers so you can identify them easily.

5. Give supplies a home
Keep only the tools you use daily within reach. Store spare pens, paper, and accessories in a small tray or reused box, grouped by purpose. A clear working area makes it easier to concentrate and lets the room return to other uses when needed.

6. Finish with a reset
At the end of the day, save your work, note the next task, and return supplies to their places. Wipe the surface when needed and take away cups. Spend a few minutes testing what feels awkward during the first week, then make small adjustments instead of buying everything immediately.
